Group Risk Management Policy

GRP-POL-001|Version6.0|Internal

## 4.Definitions

The following definitions apply throughout this policy andall subordinate risk documentation.

| TERM | DEFINITION |
|---|---|
| Risk | The effect of uncertainty ontheGroup's objectives,expressed as a combination of the consequence of an event and the likelihoodofitsoccurrence. |
| Inherent risk | Thelevel ofriskbefore consideration ofanymitigating control,assuming controls are absentor whollyineffective. |
| Residual risk | Thelevel ofriskremainingafteroperationofcontrolsassessed asdesignedand operatingeffectively. |
| Target risk | The level ofresidualrisk the Group intends to achievefollowing completion of agreed treatment actions. |
| Risk appetite | The aggregate level andtypeofrisk theGroup is willing to assume in pursuit of its strategicobjectives,approvedbythe Board. |
| Risk tolerance | The permissible variation around an appetite measure before escalation is triggered. Tolerance is narrower than the limit. |
| Risk limit | Ahardquantitativeboundarythatmustnotbebreached.Alimit breach isa policybreach. |
| Risk capacity | The maximumrisk theGroup couldabsorb given capital, liquidity,operational capabilityandregulatoryconstaints. |
| Risk owner | The named individual accountable for management ofa specific risk,includingadequacy of its controls and treatment. Recordedintheregisterbynameandemployeeidentifier—forexample,RSK-4488isownedbyNaomiK.Osadebe (EMP-41077). |
| Control owner | The named individual accountable for design,operation and testing ofa specific control. |
| Control | Ameasurethatmodifiesrisk.beingpreyentive,detective orcorrective.andeithermanual orautomated. |
| Key control | Acontrol on which primaryreliance is placed to keep a risk within appetite.Subject to mandatory independent testing. |
| lssue | An identified weakness in the design or operation of a control,or a gap between the current and required state. |
| Incident | An eventthathasoccurredandcaused,orhadpotentialtocause,loss,disruption,regulatorybreach,customer detrimentorreputationaldamage. |
| Nearmiss | Aneventwithpotentialtoresult inlossordetrimentthatdidnot doso,whetherthroughcontroloperationor through chance. |
| Loss event | An incidentresulting in quantifiable financial loss,whether or not the loss has yet been booked. |
| Keyrisk indicator (KRI) | A quantifiable measure used to monitor the level of,or change in,a risk exposure over time. |
| Keycontrolindicator（kCI） | Aguantifiablemeasure oftheoperatingperformanceofa control. |
| RCSA | RiskandControlSelf-Assessment:thestructuredprocessbywhichthefirstlineidentifiesrisks,assessescontrolsand rates residual exposure. |
| Risk acceptance | A documented,time-bound decision to tolerate a residual risk without further treatment,taken by an authorised approver. |
| Exception (waiver) | Adocumented,time-boundapproval tooperateoutside areguirementofthispolicyorasubordinatestandard. |
| Emergingrisk | Arisknewlydeveloping or changing,whose impactor likelihoodis notyetwell understoodandcannotyetbereliably quantified. |
| Important business service | Aservicedelivered toanexternal enduser,thedisruptionofwhichcouldcauseintolerableharmtocustomers ormarket integrity. |
| Impact tolerance | The maximum tolerable duration or extent of disruption to an important business service. |
| Materialrisktaker | Anindividual whoseprofessionalactivitieshave a material impactontheGroup'sriskprofile,asdefinedbythe RemunerationCommitteeandrecordedbyname,employeeidentifierandrole in theMRTRegister. |
| Personal data | Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person,including name,employee identifier,corporate or personal e-mail, telephone number,homeaddress,date ofbirth,national identifierand photographic image. |
| Three lines model Theaccountability structure separatingriskownership(first line),oversightandchallenge (second line)andindependent assurance (third line). | Three lines model |
